title: Do evidence roots mark where new evidence entered?
frozenBefore: any OpenAlex query was issued for this experiment
whyFrozenFirst: Both ground-truth signals here -- work type and retraction -- are cheap to slice many ways. A false-root rate computed after choosing which slice to report is a number chosen knowing what it produces. The slice, the criterion and the exclusions are fixed here.

dependsOn.what: a root criterion demonstrated to recover known-independent observations
dependsOn.ifThatFails: HRI-2 is answered vacuously and reports that, rather than computing a false-root rate over roots that are not measuring independence. This is registered now so the dependency cannot be quietly dropped if v0.3 is inconvenient.

groundTruth.rule: type=review is non-originative by definition; a review classified as an evidence root is a false root

groundTruth.signal: OpenAlex is_retracted, refined by retraction reason
groundTruth.rule: a retracted work whose retraction concerns data or results is a root whose evidence was never there
groundTruth.caveat: retraction is NOT wrongness. Authorship and ethics retractions may leave sound data. Reason is required; is_retracted alone is insufficient and using it alone is prohibited.

endpoints.primary: false-root rate: proportion of works classified as evidence roots that are type=review
endpoints.secondary: retraction-cascade depth: number of works transitively depending on a data-related retracted root
endpoints.H0: root status is uncorrelated with originative status; false-root rate equals the base rate of reviews in the corpus

whyTheSecondaryMattersBeyondThisHypothes: A retraction is a root-set error occurring in the world rather than in a constructed witness. T5 (root_error_tolerance, formal/lean/) states what a margin survives when the root set is disturbed by k. Retraction cascades are the first chance to observe that disturbance empirically rather than assume it.
stopRule: corpus declared before any query and not extended; if retraction reasons cannot be separated into data-related and administrative for the declared corpus, the secondary endpoint is reported as unassignable rather than computed from is_retracted alone.
prohibitedOverstatement: Do not equate retraction with error. Do not report a false-root rate without the corpus base rate of reviews beside it, since the null is that they are equal.
